name: Milford–Montague Toll Bridge
connectingPointsDisplay: Montague Township, NJ — Dingman Township, PA
facts: The Milford–Montague Toll Bridge, a 1,150‑foot truss crossing, opened December 30, 1953, replacing an 1889 structure and joining U.S. Route 206 between New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
Approved in 1951, the bridge was built alongside the Delaware Water Gap and Portland–Columbia toll bridges, with all three inaugurations spaced roughly two weeks apart in December 1953.
Tolls run only northbound into Pennsylvania, a unique policy that began when the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission first opened the bridge to traffic.
